questions.q: After a 2 g dose of a 5 % ginger extract, what form do gingerols take in human plasma?
options: Almost entirely glucuronide and sulfate conjugates, with free 6-gingerol undetectable
Mostly free aglycones at micromolar levels
Bound to albumin as unchanged gingerol for 24 hours
Converted to zingerone, which is the main circulating species
questions.why: Free 6-gingerol was undetectable at every time point; conjugates peaked at 0.47 to 0.85 µg/mL with half-lives of 1 to 3 h and no accumulation.

questions.q: How do free plasma gingerol and shogaol levels compare with the concentrations that inhibit COX-2, 5-LOX or CYP enzymes in vitro?
options: They match within a factor of two
They are equal only after heated ginger
questions.why: COX-2 IC50s are 7.5 to 32 µM; free 6-shogaol peaks near 0.05 µM after a maximal supplement dose.

questions.q: How does dried ginger powder compare with fresh rhizome in total gingerols plus shogaols per gram?
options: Dried is 3 to 8 times richer per gram
Dried contains no actives after drying
questions.why: A validated survey found 1.1 to 1.5 mg/g in fresh rhizome and 4.4 to 11.3 mg/g in dried powder, with supplements varying about 10-fold.

questions.q: Where does the commonly quoted "4 g/day limit" for ginger come from?
options: The EU monograph's maximum daily dose
The top of the German Commission E's 1990 therapeutic range
questions.why: The EMA assessment report traces 2 to 4 g/day to Commission E; the 2025 EU monograph caps motion-sickness use at 2.5 g/day and no human NOAEL exists.

questions.q: What does about 1 g/day of ginger do for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy versus placebo?
options: Reduces nausea intensity but has no reliable effect on vomiting, equivalent to vitamin B6
Reduces both by more than half
questions.why: Twelve RCTs give nausea MD 1.20 VAS points (I² = 0 %) and a non-significant vomiting effect; a 291-woman trial found equivalence to pyridoxine.

questions.q: What did the 68,522-woman Norwegian cohort find about ginger use in pregnancy?
options: No increase in malformations, stillbirth, preterm birth or low Apgar
questions.why: The cohort found no malformation or perinatal signal; the pooled RCT miscarriage estimate (RR 3.14, CI 0.65 to 15.11) is too imprecise to exclude an effect on early loss.

questions.q: What did 1.2 g of ginger do to liquid gastric emptying on antral ultrasound in healthy volunteers?
questions.why: Half-emptying time was 13.1 versus 26.7 min with placebo; the effect replicated in dyspepsia without relieving symptoms, and 0.5 to 1 g doses were null by other methods.

questions.q: How do gingerols and shogaols act on the 5-HT3 receptor?
options: As competitive antagonists at the ondansetron site
They have no action on 5-HT3 receptors
As non-competitive, allosteric inhibitors that do not bind the ondansetron site
questions.why: In human recombinant and native enteric receptors they reduce the maximal serotonin response without displacing the labelled antagonist.

questions.q: At 1 to 4 g/day of dried ginger powder, what happened to platelets, bleeding time and INR in controlled human studies?
options: Nothing changed, including in a warfarin pharmacokinetic trial
questions.why: Every controlled study at these doses was null; the warfarin trial gave an S-warfarin clearance ratio of 1.05 and unchanged INR.

questions.q: What is the source of the widely quoted "+17.7 % testosterone" effect of ginger?
options: One uncontrolled open-label pre/post study not indexed in PubMed
questions.why: No randomized placebo-controlled trial of ginger on testosterone exists in men; the figure comes from 75 Iraqi men with upper-normal baseline testosterone, no placebo and no stated dose.

questions.q: What does a single dose of ginger before or after exercise do to pain, effort and endurance?
questions.why: Acute 2 g before cycling, 2 g after eccentric exercise and 1 g before a time-to-exhaustion test were all null; four weeks of juiced ginger did not change cycling performance.

questions.q: What is the Cochrane estimate for ginger versus placebo in primary dysmenorrhea?
options: Complete pain relief in most women
About 1.5 cm lower pain on a 10 cm scale, low-quality evidence
questions.why: Three RCTs in 266 women gave MD −1.55 (95 % CI −2.43 to −0.68); 22 of 27 supplement trials were Iranian and only one was adequately blinded.

questions.q: What is the one consistent harm of ginger at trial doses?
options: Gastrointestinal effects such as heartburn and belching
questions.why: GI adverse effects are common (1 to 10 %), dose-related, grade 1 at 2 g, and doubled withdrawals in osteoarthritis trials.

questions.q: What size of CRP reduction do meta-analyses of ginger RCTs report, and in whom?
options: About 0.4 to 1.0 mg/L, almost entirely in metabolically ill cohorts
questions.why: The GRADE pool gives CRP −0.86 mg/L with high heterogeneity; no RCT of ginger alone on CRP in healthy non-obese adults was found.

questions.q: Which chemotherapy antiemetic effect of ginger is reproducible across trials?
options: Better results at 2 g on the chemotherapy day
Less acute vomiting with 0.5 to 1 g/day taken for more than 3 days, started before chemotherapy
questions.why: Pooled OR 0.3 to 0.4 for acute vomiting at ≤1 g/day; same-day 1 to 2 g was null in the two best-run trials and the 1.5 g arm did less than 0.5 to 1 g.

questions.q: For postoperative nausea and vomiting, what does ginger at or above 1 g reliably do?
options: Lowers nausea scores and rescue antiemetic use; the vomiting effect is inconsistent
questions.why: The 2006 pool gave PONV RR 0.69 on 363 patients; later pools found nausea benefit but vomiting RR 0.78 with a confidence interval crossing one.

questions.q: What dosing pattern reduced next-day exercise soreness in the foundational ginger trials?
options: 2 g/day for 11 days before the damaging bout, cutting soreness by about 23 to 25 %
A single 2 g dose right after exercise
4 g/day for 5 days, which cut soreness by half
questions.why: Raw and heated ginger gave 25 % and 23 % reductions with borderline p-values; an independent 4 g/day trial found no pain effect.

questions.q: What happened to creatine kinase, a muscle-damage marker, in ginger exercise trials?
options: It never fell, and in one trial kept rising longer with ginger
It fell only with heated ginger
questions.why: No ginger-only trial reports lower CK; the soreness effect reads as modest analgesia rather than less muscle damage.

questions.q: What is the pooled effect of ginger on knee osteoarthritis pain versus placebo?
options: SMD −0.30 with twice the withdrawal rate; ibuprofen ranked above ginger
Equal to diclofenac in every trial
questions.why: Five placebo RCTs give pain SMD −0.30 and withdrawals RR 2.33; an independent meta-analysis called the evidence insufficient.

questions.q: What is the state of the evidence for ginger lowering HbA1c in type 2 diabetes?
options: Settled: every pool agrees on a 2-point drop
Pooled Iranian trials show −0.4 to −1.0 points, but the risk-of-bias-filtered pool and the largest single trial found nothing
questions.why: Heterogeneity is 77 to 92 %, the RoB-2 pool of five trials was null, and the 204-patient trial of ginger in black tea found no glycemic change.

questions.q: Which lipid changes consistently with ginger across meta-analyses?
options: Triglycerides fall by about 9 to 25 mg/dL; cholesterol fractions barely move
questions.why: Triglycerides fall in nearly every pool; total and LDL changes are 0 to −8 mg/dL and inconsistent; all lipid outcomes are very low certainty.

questions.q: In whom does ginger lower blood pressure?
options: People with elevated pressure, by about 5/2 mmHg at 2 g/day or more; not normotensive adults
questions.why: The 2026 GRADE pool gives SBP −5.03 mmHg with the effect concentrated in elevated baseline pressure; healthy adults showed no change.

questions.q: What happened to gastric mucosal prostaglandins when osteoarthritis patients took ginger extract versus diclofenac?
options: They rose on ginger and fell on diclofenac, with mucosal damage only on diclofenac
questions.why: This is the best human evidence that ginger does not act as a systemic COX-1 inhibitor in the stomach.

questions.q: What did the only double-blind RCT of ginger in infertile men find?
options: Lower sperm DNA fragmentation, no change in count, motility and morphology trending worse, hormones measured only at baseline
questions.why: Adjusted fragmentation difference 3.21 points (p = 0.009); concentration unchanged; progressive motility and morphology both p = 0.06 against ginger; no pregnancy endpoint.

questions.q: What is known about ginger and the vestibular system in motion sickness?
options: It has no vestibular action; laboratory trials split and sea trials show less vomiting or parity with drugs
It blocks vestibular nystagmus like dimenhydrinate
It has been proven superior to scopolamine
questions.why: Ginger did not alter caloric, rotatory or optokinetic nystagmus; one rotating-chair study was positive, the next null, and no meta-analysis exists.

questions.q: Which measurable intermediate links ginger to a nausea endpoint in humans?
options: Blunted vection-induced tachygastria and vasopressin release
questions.why: In 13 susceptible volunteers, 1 and 2 g reduced vection nausea, tachygastria and plasma vasopressin but not nausea produced by intravenous vasopressin.

questions.q: What is the best human evidence for ginger-induced thermogenesis?
options: A 500 kcal/day rise in resting metabolism
A 5 kg weight loss in 4 weeks
A 43 kcal/day rise in thermic effect of food in ten overweight men, with no change in resting energy expenditure
questions.why: Weight falls 1 to 1.5 kg at 2 g/day in one pool and not at all in the larger 36-RCT pool; the meal test showed no effect on glucose, insulin or lipids.

questions.q: What does the evidence show for ginger in migraine?
options: Equivalence to sumatriptan and effective prophylaxis
Better than placebo only as an add-on to IV ketoprofen and in a feverfew combination; the only prophylaxis RCT was negative
questions.why: The 2026 GRADE synthesis rates every outcome low or very low and concludes it is too uncertain whether ginger works as acute or preventive treatment.

questions.q: Which molecule mediates ginger's effects in the body?
options: Unresolved: deconjugated metabolites, gingerdiols and gut-microbial shogaol products are proposed, none confirmed in humans
Glucuronides, shown to inhibit COX in vivo
questions.why: Over 90 % of absorbed 6-shogaol becomes phase I and cysteine-conjugated metabolites; the microbial-metabolite route rests on one mouse study.

questions.q: What did the two human colon-biopsy tests of the COX/LOX hypothesis show?
options: PGE2 fell only under one normalization in normal-risk volunteers, and leukotriene B4 rose in at-risk subjects
questions.why: The authors of the at-risk study wrote that ginger lacks the ability to decrease eicosanoid levels in that group.

questions.q: What is the main weakness of the antioxidant-biomarker evidence for ginger?
options: Effects go in opposite directions across pools
Heterogeneity of 83 to 98 % and the largest effects come from the smallest, shortest, lowest-dose trials
questions.why: MDA falls and GPx, TAC and SOD rise in every pool, but the small-study pattern and very low GRADE certainty undermine the estimate.

questions.q: What is the state of human evidence on ginger and cytochrome P450 drug interactions?
options: Proven strong CYP3A4 inhibition in patients
Ginger induces all CYP enzymes in humans
Micromolar inhibition in vitro, the only human probe (CYP2C9 with warfarin) null, gut-wall effects untested
questions.why: Free plasma levels are 100- to 1,000-fold below the in-vitro IC50s, so systemic inhibition is implausible; first-pass intestinal effects on narrow-index drugs remain possible.

questions.q: Where does the bleeding signal for ginger with anticoagulants come from?
options: Self-reported bleeding on warfarin (OR 3.20 without higher INR) and about ten case reports without rechallenge
questions.why: A 314-patient survey found no association, the EU monograph adopted no bleeding warning, and the one mechanistically plausible unresolved case is dabigatran via P-glycoprotein.

questions.q: Which pregnancy signals for ginger remain unresolved?
options: A Korean cohort stillbirth odds ratio of 7.8 with a confidence interval to 70, and more vaginal spotting in the Norwegian cohort
questions.why: Both signals are imprecise or confounded; the EU monograph keeps "preferable to avoid" as a precaution while acknowledging 300 to 1,000 reassuring outcomes.

questions.q: What characterizes the rodent evidence that ginger raises testosterone?
options: Consistent large increases in healthy animals at food doses
Mostly rescue after chemical or metabolic testicular insult, at human-equivalent doses of 0.5 to 11 g/day of extract
questions.why: In healthy rats the effect is small and inconsistent, and isolated zingerone, geraniol and 6-gingerol did not reverse the diabetic testosterone deficit.

questions.q: What does the only manometry study show about ginger and the lower esophageal sphincter?
options: Resting pressure unchanged; swallow-induced relaxation increased
questions.why: Neither "ginger causes reflux" nor "ginger cures reflux" is supported; heartburn occurs in about one user in eight in open-label series.

questions.q: Which glycemic mechanism of ginger has been demonstrated in humans?
options: Lower HOMA-IR only; GLUT4, AMPK, GLP-1 and enzyme inhibition are cell and rodent findings
questions.why: The most potent constituent on GLUT4 in cells was [8]-gingerol, not [6]-gingerol, and no human study has measured any of these pathways after ginger.

questions.q: Why is "ginger is a natural ibuprofen working in your blood" a myth?
options: Because free gingerols are undetectable or near 0.05 µM in plasma, purified gingerols showed no COX-1 inhibition, and gastric PGE2 rose on ginger extract
Because ibuprofen is also a plant extract
Because ginger has no enzyme activity in vitro
questions.why: Compound-dependent COX-2 activity at micromolar concentrations in a dish is the defensible statement; the human mechanism is not established.

questions.q: What is wrong with the claim that ginger is as effective as sumatriptan?
options: The trial used too high a dose
The 100-patient trial had no placebo arm, no non-inferiority margin and no effect sizes in its abstract
questions.why: The 2026 GRADE meta-analysis rates the comparison "very uncertain"; the doses quoted circulate only from secondary sources.

questions.q: What does the evidence say about ginger as a blood thinner at label doses?
options: It must always be stopped before surgery because trials show bleeding
Every controlled study at 1 to 4 g/day of powder was null; effects appear only at 10 g, raw ginger with fat, or litres of tea
questions.why: Pausing supplements before surgery is a cost-free precaution, not a demonstrated hazard; the dabigatran case is the one plausible unresolved interaction.

questions.q: Is fresh ginger stronger than dried, and does heating make it more anti-inflammatory?
options: No: dried holds 4.4 to 11.3 mg/g versus 1.1 to 1.5 mg/g fresh, and heated ginger matched raw in the only human comparison
Fresh is stronger but heating helps
questions.why: Drying and heating convert gingerols to shogaols rather than destroying them; heated ginger gave 23 % and raw 25 % soreness reduction.

questions.q: What is the trial evidence for ginger ale, candied ginger, lozenges or tea against nausea?
options: None exists; the positive trials used 0.5 to 1.2 g of powdered rhizome in capsules, and higher doses did less
Ginger ale is the best-studied form
questions.why: The 1.5 g chemotherapy arm did less than 0.5 to 1.0 g, the 2 g arm was null, and the pregnancy subgroup favoured under 1,500 mg/day.

questions.q: What dose of dried ginger powder carried the positive nausea trials?
options: 0.5 to 1 g/day, with higher doses doing less
questions.why: Cardiometabolic and inflammation trials used 1.5 to 2 g/day, the soreness protocol 2 g/day for 11 days, and the EU monograph caps repeated use at 2.5 g/day.

questions.q: What matters more than dose for ginger's antiemetic and soreness effects?
options: Timing: pre-loading three days before chemotherapy, one hour before travel, or 5 to 11 days before a hard session
questions.why: Same-day dosing was null in both the chemotherapy and the exercise settings; the positive trials pre-loaded.

questions.q: How much active compound can a 30 to 60 mL ginger shot contain at most?
options: About 35 to 90 mg, comparable to 1 to 2 g of dried powder, with no peer-reviewed assay of commercial shots
About 500 mg, more than any capsule
questions.why: Fresh rhizome holds 1.1 to 1.5 mg/g, so a shot is a food-range dose in the nausea band, not the 1.5 to 2 g/day of the cardiometabolic trials.

questions.q: Which interaction rules survive the evidence for ginger at 2 g/day?
options: Dangerous bleeding with any aspirin dose
Plausible additive effects with antidiabetic and antihypertensive drugs, worse acute nausea with aprepitant in one trial, and a gallstone caution resting only on rat bile data
questions.why: Label-dose anticoagulant interaction is unproven, heavy intake on a DOAC is not, and gut-wall CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein effects on narrow-index drugs are untested.
